say.en: Eight members of a family work every day on a small farm that needs only five. All eight look busy. Are all of them really employed? In this lesson: Define unemployment and name its data sources.
Distinguish open, disguised and seasonal unemployment.
Explain the government's role in employment generation.

body.en: The NSSO defines *unemployment* as a situation in which persons who, owing to lack of work, are not working but either seek work through employment exchanges, intermediaries, friends or relatives, or by applying to prospective employers, or express their willingness to work under the prevailing conditions. Data on unemployment come from the reports of the Census of India, the NSSO's surveys of employment and unemployment, and the registration of job seekers with employment exchanges.

points.en: Unemployed = not working but seeking or available for work
Sources: Census, NSSO surveys, employment exchanges

narration.en: An unemployed person is one who has no work but is looking for it or is willing to work. We get the data from the Census, from NSSO surveys and from employment exchange registrations.

say.en: First, the unemployment rate. The labour force is everyone working plus everyone seeking work.
If 9,200 people work and 800 are seeking work, the rate is 800 out of 10,000, that is 8 per cent.
Now disguised unemployment. A family farm needs five workers and produces fifty quintals.
Eight family members work on it, and the output is still fifty quintals.
The extra three add nothing. Their marginal productivity is zero: they are disguised unemployed.
To create jobs, the government acts directly, by hiring, and indirectly, by expanding output. MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of rural wage work.

title.en: Types of unemployment and government action

body.en: Open *unemployment* is when people seek work and find none. Disguised unemployment is when more people are engaged in a work than are needed, as on family farms: removing the extra workers does not reduce output. Seasonal unemployment occurs when farm work is unavailable in certain months, so many rural workers migrate to towns in the off-season. The government creates jobs directly, by employing people in its departments and public enterprises, and indirectly, as higher public output raises demand for inputs from private firms. Under MGNREGA 2005, rural households who volunteer for unskilled manual work are guaranteed 100 days of wage employment in a year.

points.en: Disguised: marginal productivity of extra workers is zero

problem.en: A town has 9,200 employed persons and 800 persons seeking work. A family farm there needs 4 workers but 7 family members work on it. Find the unemployment rate and the number disguised unemployed on the farm.

steps.en: Farm: 7 working − 4 needed = 3 workers whose removal would not reduce output.
These 3 are disguised unemployed (marginal productivity zero).

answer.en: Unemployment rate 8%; 3 disguised unemployed on the farm.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A town has 9,200 employed persons and 800 persons seeking work. A family farm there needs 4 workers but 7 family members work on it. Find the unemployment rate and the number disguised unemployed on the farm.

say.en: Let us work through this together. A town has 9,200 employed persons and 800 persons seeking work. A family farm there needs 4 workers but 7 family members work on it. Find the unemployment rate and the number disguised unemployed on the farm.
Labour force equals 9,200 plus 800 equals 10,000.
Unemployment rate equals 800 divided by 10,000 times 100 equals 8 per cent.
Farm: 7 working minus 4 needed equals 3 workers whose removal would not reduce output.
These 3 are disguised unemployed (marginal productivity zero).
So the answer is Unemployment rate 8 percent; 3 disguised unemployed on the farm.
